text.p: Italian debt markets regained their poise by late trade after a choppy session upset by EMU jitters, brokers said.
"We're in a trading range -- everyone's guessing about EMU, whether its going to be delayed or whether they'll go for the soft option," one broker at large British bank in London said.
He noted a statement by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar declaring the single currency criteria and timetable should be kept to.
"The market was a buy on the statement from Kohl and Aznar," the broker said.

But a rumour that newly elected French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin would ask President Jacques Chirac for a two-year delay to the launch of the single currency drove Btps down to the day's low before France denied the rumour.
The September LIFFE contract was trading seven basis points up at 130.55 having dipped to 130.28 earlier. Support was seen at 130.00 and resistance at 131.00.
The February 2007 Btp was finished 11 basis points weaker at 97.61 with a yield of 7.21 percent and a spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund at 139 basis points.

On the whole there was nothing much to move Italian markets from the domestic point of view and brokers said the market was consolidating as it waited for a signal from European leaders as to which way European economic and monetary union would go.
"Btps and Bunds have been tracking each other because no one knows whether EMU is going to be delayed or be soft," a broker said.
